habitat: Inland waters, where it breeds, and coasts.
summary: A common to abundant resident in Newman's account. The breeding adult has an all-grey hood, pale yellow eyes and a bright red bill and legs. The non-breeding adult has a grey smudge on the ear coverts only. The immature has the front half of the head pale grey, a darker ear-patch extending over the crown, a dark eye, and a dark-tipped bill with an orange-pink base, or rarely a wholly dark bill. The back and upperwings are grey. Newman does not describe a call. The Kemp code VB was left unchanged.

head.pattern: Grey smudge on the ear coverts only, not a full hood.

bill.shape: Usually a dark-tipped bill with an orange-pink base. A wholly dark bill is a very rare variation. Those colours are not stored as a single token.

research.note: Newman calls it a common to abundant resident, so status is resident and all twelve months are listed. The Kemp code VB was left unchanged, as were the population figures. Hartlaub’s Gull is the comparison Newman names and is not in this list. Newman does not describe the call. The immature eye is described as dark, which is not stored as an iris colour.
